newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firm on fund flows, inflation hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firm on fund flows, inflation hopes.

text.p: The Mexican peso shrugged off falls in primary rates to open marginally firmer due to foreign capital flows into the local bourse and optimistic forecasts for inflation data due later in the day, dealers said.
"The peso is holding steady despite the drop in (domestic) interest rates," a trader said, referring to Tuesday night's fall in Cetes rates at the primary auction.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both opened 0.25 of a centavo firmer at 7.8970/7.9000 and 7.8930/7.8975 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts meanwhile opened 1.7 centavos firmer at 7.8900/7.8940 per dollar.
Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates fell by 158 basis points to 18.37 percent at auction Tuesday night. This compares with an average forecast fall of 139 basis points in a Reuters survey.
The Mexican bourse's blue chip IPC index was up 35.62 points to 4,856.76 in early trade.
Banco de Mxico was expected to announce June inflation figures shortly after the close of foreign exchange trade.
A Reuters survey MEX22 of 13 Mexico City financial firms forecast an average gain of 0.90 percent in the consumer price index during June.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8900/7.9100 per dollar for the 48-hour peso during the session.
